review_cost.rationale: Approving as-is would be premature; the asks are concrete, localized and small — one focused round of changes, not structural rework.

findings.issue: Global response cache never evicts; every API resource touched (up to ~3000 records incl. all pokemon/move pages) is held in memory forever, with no size guard.
findings.suggestion: Cap the Map (e.g. simple LRU at a few hundred entries) or add a max-entry guard with an explanatory comment.

findings.issue: Pervasive `any` on API records (also views/pokemon.tsx:223-229, views/details.tsx:57, data.ts:49) defeats tsconfig strict mode and hides the data contract the views rely on.
findings.suggestion: Define minimal interfaces for the used fields of pokemon-species, pokemon, move, ability, type; type api<T>() call sites.

findings.issue: Fragment endpoints answer 404 and 500 (onError, index.tsx:93-105) with full-page documents, which htmx swaps into a table fragment target.
findings.suggestion:
Make notFound/onError HX-Request-aware: return a small fragment ('

Not found

') when isPartial(c).

findings.issue: serveStatic({ root: './dist' }) resolves against the process cwd, so npm start only works when launched from app/.
findings.suggestion: Use an absolute root derived from import.meta.dirname (or pathToFileURL) so the server is location-independent.

findings.issue: Direct navigation to /pokemon/:name/moves (the fragment URL) returns a bare fragment with no document shell, contrary to htmx's 'public URL should return a complete document' guidance.
findings.suggestion: Either reuse the isPartial() branch to return the full pokemon page for non-hx requests, or mark these as non-public fragment routes.

findings.issue: mainTypes() carries full type records (incl. every Pokémon list) to consumers that only need name/label (TypesPage, typeLabels, HomePage select), inflating cache and blurring the boundary.
findings.suggestion: Split into a lightweight typeList() (name+label) and keep record access inside typesByPokemonId().

findings.issue: Every sort click re-runs loadPokemon + loadMoves (all move fetches for the game) just to re-render one table; wasteful though masked by the cache.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable with the cache, but consider caching per (pokemon, game) rows in memory or sorting client-side from the already-rendered table.

findings.issue: The aria-live='polite' div is replaced via outerHTML swap; replacing the live region itself typically suppresses announcements.
findings.suggestion: Keep the #results container static and swap its inner content (hx-swap innerHTML) so the live region persists.

summary: This is idiomatic, current-release Hono + htmx done the way the docs actually teach it — jsxRenderer, fragment/full-page dual rendering keyed on HX-Request with correct history-restore handling, and hx-sync race control. The structure is clean and the shared components earn their keep; the costs are an unbounded in-memory cache, `any`-typed API records, and fragment endpoints that return whole documents on errors. I'd request one focused round of changes and then merge.
